# Test fixtures

Real artifacts copied verbatim from `data/extracted/`, so Go tests never need
Python, the source PDFs, or the network. Regenerate with `make extract` and
re-copy if the extractor's output contract changes.

"Copied verbatim" is the property everything here rests on, and it is checkable:
each page fixture's sha256 equals the one `data/extracted/<doc>/manifest.json`
records for the artifact it came from. A test that passes against these
fixtures therefore passes against the real corpus. Do not hand-edit one — a
fixture that has drifted from the extraction is a test that proves nothing about
what `fisc build` will read.

Page fixtures are `.txt`, not `.md`, for the same reason `data/extracted/`
switched: `pdftotext -layout` encodes the printed column grid in runs of
spaces, and GitHub's blob view renders markdown and collapses them.

Every fixture page carries **both** substrates — `pages/<doc>-pNNNN.txt` and
`geometry/<doc>-pNNNN.json`. A document holding one without the other is not a
shape the extractor can produce, so building one in a test would let it pass
against a corpus that cannot exist.

Each fixture is here because it encodes a specific failure mode found while
validating the approach — none is a generic sample.

## Pages

| Fixture | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/budget-p0066.txt` | Budget Book p66 | The citywide spine. Every control total ties to this page. Rows are "label followed by 4 numbers" (2 fund groups × 2 fiscal years), and it is the **label anchor** for p67. It also carries the running footer `BUDGET FY 2025-27 … Page 62`, whose bare page number parses as an amount — which is why every block on this page states a `stop_at`. |
| `pages/budget-p0067.txt` | Budget Book p67 | The spine's continuation, and the nastiest case in the corpus: **no row labels at all** — identity is positional from p66, so a single missing row mismaps every row beneath it. This fixture is also the evidence for `fisc-c00`: it used to carry nine revenue rows because xberg's `strip_repeating_text` deleted the third of three identical all-dash rows, and the count assertion (72 ≠ 80) is what caught it. Any mapping engine must fail loudly here, not guess. |
| `pages/budget-p0167.txt` | Budget Book p167 | General Fund expenditures by department × object category, and the page with the **tightest line structure in the corpus**: the smallest gap between two printed lines is 7.99pt against a 4.16pt clustering tolerance, and the gap in question is a wrapped department name (`Devel`) sitting immediately above a data row. It is where a *wrapped label lands between a row's figures and the next row's label* (`fisc-0cs`), and it carries the city's own misspelling — the heading prints `INNOVATION & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT` and the total row `DEVELOPEMENT`, with `TOTAL` wrapped onto the next line, so a rollup anchor cannot be derived from the heading. Six divisions are read from it by rules today. |
| `pages/budget-p0076.txt` | Budget Book p76 | The transfer schedule, and the fixture that retired a bead's premise: it was believed unextractable and slated for hand transcription until poppler replaced xberg, and it is 22 ordinary labelled rows. It is here for three things at once — a row whose identity is **two printed fields** (`Transfer From X … to Y`) separated by an arbitrary run of spaces, which `Row.Label` cannot express without encoding the page's kerning; a **footnote marker** trailing every data row — `(1)` through `(10)`, keyed to the descriptions at the foot of the page — which `amount.Parse` reads as a *parenthesised negative* because that is how these documents write one; and a second `fisc-0cs` wrapped label (`Connection`) outside the department pages. Its budget columns tie to the printed total to the cent and its historical columns miss by millions, so it is also the counter-example to "declare the difference and move on". |
| `pages/budget-p0168.txt` | Budget Book p168 | The two-level rounding chain the rollup design rests on. `ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES TOTAL` is $6,311,564 and so is the sum of its three printed division `Total`s, while the six **object rows** beneath them give $6,311,563 — Finance's own dollar is absorbed by its printed subtotal and reappears one level up. A rollup summing leaves ties or fails depending on whether the document's roundings happen to cancel, which is why `File.Rollups` sums printed totals instead (`fisc-3bl`). It is also the page carrying the schedule's only `Debt Services` row, and the tail of a division whose head is on p167. |
| `pages/budget-p0169.txt` | Budget Book p169 | The only page in the schedule that is both a **tail and a head**: Special Operations' last object row and printed `Total` close a division that began on p168, and Environmental Services opens one that finishes on p170. It also carries three of the four wrapping division labels — `Community`/`Development Admin`, `Housing & Human`/`Services`, `Public Works`/`Administration` — each landing between one row's figures and the next row's label (`fisc-0cs`), and two of the four declared `stated_total_deltas`, with opposite signs. |
| `pages/budget-p0170.txt` | Budget Book p170 | The schedule's closing total, `General Fund Total Expenses`, which is what ties the department axis to the citywide spine: $144,650,802 and $149,014,579 are p66's `TOTAL EXPENDITURES` for the General Fund to the cent. It is also the corpus's tightest anchor problem — Fire Administration prints **one** object row, so its own `Total` and `FIRE DEPARTMENT TOTAL` are three statements of one figure inside a nine-line window — and it carries `PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT TOTAL`, the one department total that is not its heading plus `" TOTAL"`. |
| `pages/budget-p0127.txt` | Budget Book p127 | General Fund revenue by source, and the **contra-revenue** case: ERAF and RPTTF are negative rows (~26% of gross property tax) that a Sankey cannot render as links. Also shows the 4-column shape (FY23-24 actual, FY24-25 revised, FY25-26, FY26-27) that makes every revenue line a trend series. |
| `pages/budget-p0128.txt` | Budget Book p128 | The page that proves `fisc-2sd`'s page list counts the wrong thing. It carries **two** discrepant blocks, not one — `Total Other Taxes` +$1 and `Total Licenses & Permits` -$2, opposite signs — so a declaration keyed by page cannot express it. `Other Taxes` also arrives here as the schedule's first **row straddle**: twelve of its fourteen rows are on p127. |
| `pages/budget-p0129.txt` | Budget Book p129 | The longest block in the corpus — `Charges for Services`, twenty rows read label by label with nothing but the whitespace gap guarding them — and the head of the strangest one: `Contributions Outsourced` prints its heading and its single row here and its printed `Total` on the next page, which is a shape no `total_spans_parts` rule in the tree has yet had to express. |
| `pages/budget-p0130.txt` | Budget Book p130 | Three anchor problems at once. `Total Contributions Outsourced` is the first line after the column header and belongs to a block with **no rows on this page**. `Miscellaneous Revenue` occurs three times — section heading, a row label inside its own block, and its total — so no unique-match anchor resolves it. And `Total General Fund` is a **rollup**, covering ten category rules; measured, it ties exactly in all four columns while five of those ten rules carry their own declared dollar, which is the two-level chain `File.Rollups` exists for, restated on the revenue side. |
| `pages/budget-p0131.txt` | Budget Book p131 | The first Other Funds page and the one `Row.Kind` was promoted for: Stormwater and Wastewater print revenue rows **and** a `Transfers In` row inside one printed `Total <fund>`, so kind is per row and the total is kind-blind. | `pages/budget-p0132.txt` | Budget Book p132 | A **fund-group boundary mid-page** — Enterprise ends and Capital begins at line 46 — so a rule cannot assume a page belongs to one group. It also carries the `Water` family: `Water`, `Water Replacement`, `Water Connection Fees` and `Wastewater Connection Fees`, where the string `Water` occurs six times and the heading is the first. |
| `pages/budget-p0133.txt` | Budget Book p133 | The **unindented layout**. pp.131/132/134/135/139/140 indent both headings and rows by six spaces; p133 and pp.136-138 print them at the left margin, so each page's geometry grid is its own and a column guard tuned on one does not transfer. Its fund names are also the corpus's worst for a blind numeric scan — `Park Fee - AB 1600`, `2022 COP Construction Fund`, `County Meas BB-Bike/Pedestrian` all carry digits or a `-`, which this corpus spells zero. |
| `pages/budget-p0134.txt` | Budget Book p134 | **Three fund-group boundaries on one page** — Capital, then Debt Service, then Permanent — and the corpus's only **Permanent Funds** section (`fisc-u8o`): pp.66-67 have no column for it, and `Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow` is $19,533 in FY2024 and zero in both budget years, which is what keeps it from breaking the six-group tie. It is also `fisc-u54`'s worked example, truncating to within one word of its same-type sibling `Doolan Canyon Open Space` (470 and 471). |
| `pages/budget-p0135.txt` | Budget Book p135 | The Special Revenue run opens, and it is the longest run in the schedule — 38 of the 69 funds. | `pages/budget-p0136.txt` | Budget Book p136 | `Police Evidence`, the section that names no fund the appendix lists: it is fund 211, `Asset Seizure - County`, and the identification is arithmetic rather than a lookup (`fisc-nne`, `fisc-8dz`). Four of its eight funds are **zero in both budget years** and non-zero in the historical columns, so dropping any of them would leave the spine tie green — which is the hole `fisc-u54` exists to close. |

It is the mirror of p129's Contributions Outsourced, and between them they are why `fisc-u2v` DEFECT 4's list of six straddles is four. ## Geometry

`pdftotext -bbox` word boxes, one file per fixture page, read by `internal/geom`
and by the resolver's column guard. Each is `[x0, y0, x1, y1, "text"]` per word,
in points, y increasing downward.

| Fixture | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `geometry/budget-p0066.json` | Budget Book p66 | The labelled half of the spine. Four columns, and the page whose worst intra-line y0 spread (0.96pt against a 4.55pt tolerance) sets the floor the line grouping has to tolerate — and that one cluster is a mixed label/header line, `EXPENDITURES: General Fund Enterprise Funds`, not a data row. |
| `geometry/budget-p0067.json` | Budget Book p67 | The label-less half, and the fixture the column guard is proved on: eight columns, 24 data lines, every one carrying exactly eight value words including four byte-identical all-dash rows. Its header line prints `FY 2025-26 / FY 2026-27` once per fund group and nowhere else on the page, which is what lets a rule name its columns without an ordinal. |
| `geometry/budget-p0076.json` | Budget Book p76 | The second substrate for the transfer schedule, and the evidence that nothing is missing from the first: the page prints two unusually wide vertical gaps (21pt where rows are otherwise 13pt apart) and geometry shows they are whitespace, not dropped rows. It is read by no test beyond the verbatim-copy check: it is committed because the page-text fixture's 22 rows are only trustworthy while the second substrate agrees, and the day something disputes them this is what settles it. |
| `geometry/budget-p0168.json` | Budget Book p168 | The second substrate for the division reads, and the evidence that the page-text fixture is not missing a row: pp.167-170 print `-` in every zero cell, so every object row carries exactly four value words and a short row would be a dropped figure rather than a blank. Committed for the same reason p76's is — the 18 object rows are only trustworthy while the second substrate agrees. |
| `geometry/budget-p0169.json` | Budget Book p169 | The wrapped-label geometry. Three division labels wrap here, and the tail sits on its own line between two data rows; `-bbox` is what shows those tails are label text at the label column's x-extent rather than a value that lost its row. |
| `geometry/budget-p0170.json` | Budget Book p170 | The closing page, committed so all four pages of the schedule carry both substrates. Its two object rows are the sparsest in the schedule and the one place a mis-filed column would be least visible by eye. |
| `geometry/budget-p0127.json` | Budget Book p127 | The four-column **labelled** shape, so the guard's labelled path is exercised against a real page rather than only against p66's four columns inside a padded block. |
| `geometry/budget-p0167.json` | Budget Book p167 | The evidence for the filing rule. This page's `FY 2025-26` header spans x 421.99–469.01 while every figure under it *ends* at 477.8–477.9 — the figures are right-aligned to a grid offset ~+9pt right of the header text, so filing a value by whether it overlaps its header places none of them, and the tokens it loses are zero dashes. |
| `geometry/budget-p0128.json` … `geometry/budget-p0140.json` | Budget Book pp.128-140 | The second substrate for the revenue schedule, one file per page because the grid is **per page and not per schedule**: pp.131/132/134/135/139/140 indent headings and rows by six spaces and pp.133/136/137/138 print them at the left margin, so a column guard proved on one layout says nothing about the other. They are committed for the reason p76's and p168's are — every row on these fourteen pages carries exactly four value words, with `-` printed in every zero cell, so a short row would be a dropped figure rather than a blank, and the page-text fixtures' 231 rows are only trustworthy while the second substrate agrees. |

### ACFR

| Fixture | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/acfr-p0177.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0177.json` | ACFR p177 | The ten-year schedule of outstanding debt, and the page behind this project's most-cited claim — `amount.TestLeadingMinusIsReallyPositive`, which `docs/review-loop-evidence.md` carries as the worked example of proving a reading with arithmetic. That test reconciles a row **transcribed into its own comment**, and the transcription is of what *xberg* produced: a `-512,946` with an empty column's dash glued to the front. Poppler reads the row with the dashes standing alone, and no token of that shape survives anywhere in the corpus. Committed so the claim rests on the page. It earns its place twice over: nine of its ten rows tie to the city's printed total exactly and **FY2024 is short by $176,292, exactly its own Financed Purchases column** — a whole column missing from a total, not the ≤$5 rounding `fisc-2sd` declares. It also prints a **standalone `$`** before each figure of its FY2016 row. That used to be described here as "a live `fisc-yun` … so the resolver cannot read this page at all", and **both halves were false**: `fisc-yun` closed at `dde657b`, and `dropCurrencyMarks` reads a lone mark in the labelled path. The percentage that once stopped the resolver reading this page at all is now the first consumer of the **quantity channel** (`fisc-9tn4`): `acfr-p0177-debt-by-type` reads all ten value columns — col 9 `quantity: percentage`, col 10 `quantity: amount_per_unit` — and publishes nothing (`fisc-xmh2`, `fisc-7jtl`). Delete col 9's declaration and the read goes red with `row "2016" column 9: cannot parse amount "2.5%": not a recognized number`, pinned by `TestACFRDebtPercentageColumnNeedsItsQuantity`; delete col 10's and **nothing objects**, because `$ 1,009` per capita is well-formed money — the hazard `fisc-9tn4` was settled on, pinned by `TestACFRDebtPerCapitaParsesCleanlyAsAmount` and tracked as `fisc-54vn`. The geometry fixture is what proves the page **cannot carry the column guard**: the footnote `(1)` is its own `-layout` line but clusters into its sentence's geometry line, 23 text lines against 22 (`TestACFRDebtPageCannotCarryTheColumnGuard`). |
| `pages/acfr-p0041.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0041.json` | ACFR p41 | THE SECOND DOCUMENT IN THE FACT STORE. The General Fund's Statement of Revenues, Expenditures And Changes In Fund Balances, printed **in millions to two decimals** — so the least significant printed digit is $10,000 and `units: millions` is not the same claim as the caption's word. The page prints **four blocks**, of which `mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml` maps three whole — revenue, Other Financing Sources and the fund balances — and the fourth, expenditure, only in part: 20 facts in all, and this fixture carries the evidence for every decision it makes. **The revenue block ties to 157.20 exactly** and was unreadable until `fisc-hcus` landed: a bare `0.0` sits on a line of its own between the last data row and the printed total, belonging to no row label. It now carries an `unmapped_text` declaration — and the same change refused the DISHONEST route, because `wrapped_labels: ["0.0"]` parsed, resolved all ten rows and tied, with nothing objecting, until the parser was taught to refuse a wrapped label that `amount.Parse` accepts. Its first row also prints a **standalone `$`** before each figure, which looks like a second blocker and is not: `fisc-yun` is closed and `dropCurrencyMarks` reads straight through it. **The expenditure block ties exactly at the top level** (137.01) over its ten printed rows; descend past the `General Government:` subtotal into its five children and it is 0.01 short, and that 0.01 is **this corpus's only consumer of a document-derived tolerance** (`fisc-1wr.2`). Reaching it needed `fisc-h96o`, because the subtotal is printed ABOVE its own rows. The block's other nine top-level rows stay unmapped, and **not all for the same reason**: six are the ACFR's remaining functions (Fire, Police, Public Works, Community Development, Economic Development, Library), which are departments `fact-departments-resolve` cannot accept (`fisc-xudn`), while Capital Outlay, Principal and Interest and fiscal charges are not departments at all and are blocked by nothing. The five rows that ARE mapped carry no department either, because two of them name departments covering several divisions. **The FY2024 column is present and skipped**: three of the four blocks the page PRINTS miss in it — revenue by $200,000, expenditure by $100,000 and the fund balances by $100,000, with only Other Financing Sources tying — and the General Government sub-block, which is inside the expenditure block and is not one of the four, misses by $170,000 on top of that. It is also the page whose **geometry pairing fails** — that orphan `0.0` sits 0.32pt below the row above, inside the line tolerance, so `-bbox` gives 51 lines against `-layout`'s 52 and no column guard is available here at all, which is why the tolerance above stands over the least-guarded figures in the corpus. |
| `pages/acfr-p0054.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0054.json` | ACFR p54 | The **audited** Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances for the governmental funds — the statement whose name MD&A's condensed, in-millions table on p41 shares, which is exactly the confusion this fixture exists to guard against: the `p167-does-not-tie-to-p41` caveat once cited p41 by the audited statement's bare name, telling readers the audited ACFR disagreed with p167 when it agrees to the dollar. **No rule maps this page** — its `FUND BALANCES- ENDING $ 87,043,576` for the General Fund is fixture-only evidence, not a fact — and `TestP167ComponentsTieToP54NotP41` re-derives from these bytes that p167's five 2025 General Fund components sum to that figure while p41's `87.10` is not where it rounds. |
| `pages/acfr-p0167.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0167.json` | ACFR p167 | Fund Balances of Governmental Funds, the Statistical Section's clean table and the first of it to publish (`fisc-oakx.3`, scope `acfr-fund-balances`). Two blocks with **identical row labels except one** — All Other Governmental Funds prints no Assigned line — which is what `TestACFRFundBalancesWrongBlockIsRefused` turns into the wrong-fund proof: either rule over the other block goes red on that row's presence or absence. Its totals lines print a **detached `$` per column** (`$ 47,139,536`), the shape `amountRun` had to learn to drop; revert that and both rules fail on "no run of 10 consecutive amounts". Both blocks tie to their printed totals exactly in all ten columns. |
| `pages/acfr-p0168.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0168.json` | ACFR p168 | Changes in Fund Balances, first page: the revenue and expenditure blocks (tying to their printed totals exactly, all ten columns each) and the three-line wrapped label **"Excess of Revenues / over (under) / expenditures"**, mapped as a section anchor plus a two-anchor row. The excess is the batch's corroboration tie — `excess-of-revenues-identity` recomputes it from the published rows per column, and it holds in all ten. Also carries the interior group heading `Debt service funds:`, consumed as the first anchor of a two-anchor row over `Principal`. |
| `pages/acfr-p0169.txt` + `geometry/acfr-p0169.json` | ACFR p169 | Changes in Fund Balances, second page: read whole, publishing nothing (`fisc-qyrw`) — the block's printed total's 2023 cell is a **copy of 2022** (components sum to 39,259,064 against a printed (1,767,367)), and so is Net change 2023. Its last row is the whole-row quantity channel's real-page consumer, the proof `fisc-oakx.2` left owed: remove the `quantity: percentage` override and the read goes red on `cannot parse amount "6.6%"` (`TestACFRChangesRowQuantityIsLoadBearing`). |

### CIP

| Fixture | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/cip-p0029.txt` + `geometry/cip-p0029.json` | CIP p29 | `fisc-j5p`: the page prints one figure of $21,130,083 as **`$21130 083`**, two whitespace-delimited tokens, so `amount.Parse("$21130")` succeeds and the rest of the row shifts one place. `internal/amount`'s digit-splitting guard cannot see it, because the split falls across a token boundary. Geometry can: both tokens' right edges (280.45 and 299.67) fall in the same column band, which ends at 301.54. The whole row is shattered this way — `$ 6 190 000` is four words — so it is also the corpus's worst case for a substrate that has lost its thousands separators. |
| `pages/cip-p0040.txt` + `geometry/cip-p0040.json` | CIP p40 | The sparse grid, and the limit of what geometry can do. Row `PB200654` prints two figures with six columns between them and `-layout` emits exactly two tokens, which is the mis-filing this whole guard exists to prevent. But the page *prints* a `-` in each of those six columns and **those dashes are in no substrate at all** — not `-layout`, `-raw`, the default mode, or `-bbox` — because they are drawn as non-text, while `PB200429` on the same page does carry its dashes. So the row fails closed and cannot be read (`fisc-8ln`). |

## Projections

| Fixture | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `sankey.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 66–67, FY2026 | The frozen `sankey.json` contract as a worked example — real figures, real fact ids, all four `link.kind` values, and both `derived: true` nodes. Hand-derived in Wave 0 so `internal/export` and `site/app.js` could be built before `internal/project` existed. Once the Go projection lands it must reproduce this byte-for-byte; until then it is the only thing pinning the contract. See [`docs/sankey-contract.md`](../docs/sankey-contract.md).  **Regenerated once, on 2026-08-29, to add `locators`** — there is no `-update` flag in this repo and there deliberately is not one, so it was done with a temporary `os.WriteFile` inside `TestSankeyReproducesGoldenFile` and reverted. That weakens the independent-derivation property unless the diff is READ, and it was: the diff is purely additive, and all 58 added locator blocks were checked against `fixture_test.go`'s two-line `spinePage` rule (general/enterprise → 66, everything else → 67) — 26 on p66, 32 on p67, zero violations. Do not regenerate it again without a rule that cheap to check against. |
| `fund-flows.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 127–140 + 167–170, FY2026 | **A CAPTURE, NOT A DERIVATION**, as is every projection fixture below it: the page fixtures are copied verbatim from artifacts whose sha256 is recorded, `sankey.golden.json` is hand-derived, and this one is Go's own output. A hand-authored table of 18 pages of schedules would be a second transcription of what the mapping rules already read, and any error in it would be invisible. It is here because the client's tests have no Go and no `facts.jsonl`, and laying THIS document out is the only evidence that the fold in `site/app.js` makes the drill-down drawable. `TestTheFundFlowsFixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` compares it line for line with what `buildProjections` builds at `fund-flows`, `metadata.generated_by` excepted, so it cannot drift from the document the site serves. Re-capture from the `bin/<fixture>-rebuilt.json` the test writes on a difference, and read the diff. **Check a recapture rather than trust it**: re-derive every link's locators from `facts/facts.jsonl`, and every link's `value_cents` as the sum of its cited facts' `amount_cents`. See [`docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md`](../docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md). |
| `fund-flows-2027.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 127–140 + 167–170, FY2027 | The second spine year's drill: each year opens into its own fund-flows document, so a drill measured over FY2026's capture alone leaves FY2027's with nothing able to see it go wrong. **Same facts, different shape** — `fund/207` (Local Housing Trust) prints $5,500,000 in the FY2026 column and `-` in this one, so its zero flow is not drawn and the document is one node and its links short of FY2026's. `TestTheFundFlows2027FixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `fund-flows-2027`; re-capture and check it as its FY2026 twin, adding that every cited fact is FY2027 adopted. |
| `sankey-2027.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 66–67, FY2027 | The spine's second column, a capture like the fund-flows fixtures, held at `sankey-2027` by `TestTheSankey2027FixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws`. It exists because the chart's residual node reads the spine, and the two columns differ exactly where `internal/check`'s declared residual endpoints say they do — FY2027 general's change in working capital is a `fund-balance/contribution` out (2,351,098) where FY2026's is a draw in (1,034,154) — so a check over FY2026's spine twice would never see that endpoint carried. |
| `department-spending.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 85–125 (upper block), FY2026 | The capture the spine's object categories open into. Each of the four object categories is one opened view, and the four are not the same shape — they reach different numbers of divisions. `TestTheDepartmentSpendingFixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `department-spending`. Check a recapture on the fund-flows rules: every link's `value_cents` the sum of its cited facts, every cited fact FY2026 adopted. |
| `department-spending-2027.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 85–125 (upper block), FY2027 | The second column of the same block, and it carries the one thing FY2026's cannot show: p0067 publishes 130,502,087 of services-and-supplies where these pages' division rows come to 130,252,087, so the object-category window draws a declared 250,000 gap mark here and none in FY2026 (`structure.BudgetBookExceptions`'s `p0067-internal-service-is-250000-high-by-object`). Capital-outlay also reaches one division fewer. `TestTheDepartmentSpending2027FixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `department-spending-2027`; check a recapture as its FY2026 twin. |
| `department-funding.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 85–125, FY2026 | The capture the fund-departments window is measured over. `TestTheDepartmentFundingFixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `department-funding`. |
| `department-funding-2027.golden.json` | Budget Book pp. 85–125, FY2027 | The same over the other spine year, because the two years decompose different funds. `TestTheDepartmentFunding2027FixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `department-funding-2027`. |
| `transfers-by-fund.golden.json` | Budget Book p. 76, FY2026 | **The one shape no other fixture can stand in for**: every other document here draws one ribbon per printed cell, and this one draws TWO per printed figure — a receiving leg keyed to the destination fund and a paying leg keyed to the payer, carrying the same `transfer_id` and citing the same `(doc_id, page, offset)`. A harness handed any other capture would measure a chart whose ribbons sum to the schedule rather than to twice it. It is what the spine's `transfers/in` opens into. `TestTheTransfersByFundFixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `transfers-by-fund`. Check a recapture on the fund-flows rules plus two this shape adds: every `transfer_id` names exactly two legs of equal value, and the two share one printed offset and are one `transfer_in` and one `transfer_out`. **The eye-checkable rule is the tie**: the receiving legs and the paying legs each sum to p76's printed grand total of $21,525,997, the spine's `transfers/in` to the cent. |
| `transfers-by-fund-2027.golden.json` | Budget Book p. 76, FY2027 | The second budget column of the same page. p76 prints different figures in the two columns, so this one ties to **$21,624,633** and a harness driven over one capture twice could not see a year join to the wrong document. The rows that print a dash in **both** budget columns draw no ribbon in either and survive in `facts_uncited`. `TestTheTransfersByFund2027FixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws` holds it at `transfers-by-fund-2027`; check a recapture as its FY2026 twin. |
| `rungs.json` | Every published column, every declared step | **Not a capture and not a document: Go's answer, and the page's input.** `rungsOf` walks each step's document from every node the chart offers, for every published year, and writes for each rung every column the step declares in draw order, every node the document reaches there, and the marks no page prints — each with its tier and its cents. **It is SERVED**: `buildAll` ships it at the site root, and `site/app.js`'s `heldFor` reads `draws[].ids` and `carryResidual`/`markGap` read `marks`; the page derives neither. So regenerating it changes what the site draws. It is UNFOLDED — no cap applied, no column dropped — because what a column holds is a fact about the documents and how much of it fits is not (AGENTS.md, "Go vets, JavaScript renders"). `TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes` pins it byte for byte to what `buildAll` serves, writing `bin/rungs-rebuilt.json` and printing the `cp -f` on a difference; `TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatTheReachPrimitivesAnswer` recomputes every column and mark from `export.ReachOf`, `ResidualOf` and `GapOf`. |
| `index.golden.html` | The served spine page, both published years | **The page as `fisc export` writes it at `index.html`**, and the DOM the client tests under `site/` are built on: `window.FISC_CONFIG` is read out of it and every element `site/app.js` paints into is found in it. It is pinned rather than assembled because the template is the only spelling of the page. `TestTheServedPageIsWhatGoRenders` holds it byte for byte to what the export writes, the build stamp blanked in both places it appears (the config's `exported_by` and the footer); on a difference the served page is written to `bin/index.golden-rebuilt.html` and the test prints the `cp -f`. Regenerating it changes what the client tests see, so read the diff. |
| `fy2026-adopted.column.json` | Budget Book pp. 66–67, 76, 85–125, 127–140, 167–170, FY2026 | **The column document the page fetches**, not a projection: `internal/export`'s `ColumnDoc`, one node table and one schedule per projection stating this fiscal year and basis, each schedule's links indexed into the shared table. `site/app.js`'s `loadColumn` fetches this shape and `scheduleOf` turns one schedule back into a document, so a client test driven over a projection golden would drive a path no browser takes. `TestTheColumnArtifactsAreWhatGoEncodes` holds it byte for byte to what `fisc export` writes at the site root as `fy2026-adopted.json`, `generated_by` blanked; on a difference it writes `bin/fy2026-adopted.column-rebuilt.json` and prints the `cp -f`. Its `generated_by` and `index.golden.html`'s `exported_by` are the same stamp, which is what lets a test serve both without the client refusing a cached copy. |
| `fy2027-adopted.column.json` | The same pages, FY2027 | The second column the page fetches, pinned the same way, because the two are not the same shape — `fund/207` is a node in one and not the other, capital-outlay reaches a different number of divisions, and only FY2027 carries the declared 250,000 gap — so a client test driven over one column twice could not see a year join to the wrong document. |
